text:
Vancouver is 6-19-1 with 13 points, and our race model gives the Canucks no realistic path to the playoffs, projecting about 60 points. Manny Malhotra's first season behind the bench has been rough by every measure: 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), a 40% share at 5v5 and 4.38 goals against a game.

The story now is what comes next. Elias Pettersson's name is in steady trade talk, including reporting from Elliotte Friedman, and he is out with an upper-body injury. The club already moved Max Sasson to the Rangers for a 2029 pick. Brock Boeser had three assists in one game this weekend, and Marco Rossi scored twice in Saturday's shootout win over Minnesota.

Sunday's 6-3 loss to Chicago summed up the rest: down 4-0 before the Canucks had a shot, and 0-for-5 on the power play, as Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis noted. Kevin Lankinen is 0-4-0 with a .833 save rate over his last five starts, 5.9 goals worse than expected, and the Filip Hronek and Zeev Buium pair has had just 32% of the expected goals. There is some bad luck in the goals against (11.85 more than the chances predict), but not enough to hide the gap.

What to watch: Pettersson's health, and whether the trade talk around him turns into a trade.
headline: Canucks bottom out as Pettersson talk grows
